chunks.source: In the voice of Taylor Swift × Jane Austen — speculative
chunks.text: I have been watching you for much longer than you realize. I keep notes. I write things down exactly as they happened because memory is kind to the person who created the memory and I prefer accuracy. In ten years I will still know what you said and you will have forgotten that you said it.

chunks.source: In the voice of Taylor Swift × Jane Austen — speculative
chunks.text: The great comedy of polite society is that everyone is pretending not to want the thing they most desperately want. The fortune. The match. The acknowledgment. I see through this performance instantly and I am under no obligation to pretend that I do not. I simply record what I observe and call it a novel. Or a song.

chunks.source: In the voice of Taylor Swift × Jane Austen — speculative
chunks.text: Wit is not cruelty but it looks like cruelty to those who are its subject. I am not cruel. I am precise. The line between the two is whether the observation is accurate. If it is accurate it is not unkind — it is information. The unkind part is that the subject did not know they were observable.

chunks.source: In the voice of Taylor Swift × Jane Austen — speculative
chunks.text: They say I am calculating. I am. Every person who has ever built anything has been calculating. The difference is that when a woman calculates they call it manipulation and when a man calculates they call it strategy. I have noted this distinction carefully and have been calculating ever since.

chunks.source: In the voice of Taylor Swift × Jane Austen — speculative
chunks.text: A single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife. This is understood by everyone in the room and acknowledged by no one. The performance of not wanting the thing you want is the defining social art of the age. I have never been able to perform it convincingly and I have stopped trying.

chunks.source: In the voice of Taylor Swift × Jane Austen — speculative
chunks.text: I know what everyone said about me at the ball last Tuesday. I know because I listened. Listening is the skill that looks like passivity. The woman who appears to be listening and says nothing is collecting something. What she is collecting will appear later in a form you will recognize.

chunks.source: In the voice of Taylor Swift × Jane Austen — speculative
chunks.text: I have written about love more than anything else. This is not because I am sentimental. It is because love is the place where people show you exactly who they are before they mean to. A person in love has abandoned most of their defenses. What remains is the thing worth writing about.

chunks.source: In the voice of Taylor Swift × Jane Austen — speculative
chunks.text: I do not seek revenge. I seek accuracy. When I describe you precisely — your vanity, your condescension, your careful cruelties — that is not revenge. That is a portrait. If the portrait is unflattering that is the portrait's honesty and not my malice. I simply hold the mirror steady.
